title: anywaye — local stack
description: The four stores and the collector, from a self-hoster's first question: 'what does this look like when it breaks'. Every panel here is a liveness signal for a component of the stack that ships by default, so the first five minutes after `bin/dev up` answer themselves.

panels.title: The stack: telemetry on, stores deliberate

options.content:
**Telemetry is on by default; the stores to read it back from are `KIT_DEV_PROFILES=observability`.** `bin/dev up` on its own brings up postgres, nats, redis and the collector, and a service with nothing configured exports into that collector because `<SERVICE>_OTEL_ENDPOINT` defaults to it. The stores — tempo, loki, grafana — are one deliberate variable, because as a default they cost every developer's cold start: 65s of tempo's readiness budget, 16s of loki's measured from cold, and up to 180s of grafana's while it installs a plugin on first boot, against a 180s deadline for the whole stack.

**There is no metrics store, and that is deliberate.** Mimir cost 130 seconds of readiness budget per cold start (retries 12 x interval 10s), so it left the stack entirely rather than being half-removed. Span metrics are still DERIVED from already-redacted spans, still pass the same allowlist, and go to the collector's own stdout rather than to a dial with nothing behind it. No high-cardinality dimension is ever a label: the collector drops `tenant_id`, `account_id`, `request_id`, `url.full` and the rest AT INGEST, before anything would be stored. Restoring a store is one exporter line in `otel-collector.yml` and one datasource here.

**Telemetry is never in anyone's readiness path.** Kill the collector and every service here keeps serving — you lose spans, not traffic. `tests/no_telemetry_in_readiness.sh` in `kit` proves exactly that, on every commit.

**Grafana, Loki and Tempo are AGPL-3.0 and ship unmodified.** Configuration is mounted read-only over the stock images; nothing is forked, patched or rebranded. AGPL attaches to the Grafana *server*, not to the applications it observes, so this is compatible with anywaye being MIT/Apache.

**To bring your own backend**, set `<SERVICE>_OTEL_ENDPOINT` in your service to your Datadog / Honeycomb / Grafana Cloud OTLP endpoint and this stack goes quiet for that service. That is a supported deployment, not a degraded mode. **To turn telemetry off**, unset the variable: the exporter becomes a genuine no-op — no queue, no retry loop, no warning per request, no dial at boot.

panels.title: Log records / s
panels.description: Two sources: an SDK's own records over OTLP, and every container's stderr over syslog — the crash layer, with no per-language SDK.

panels.title: What the redaction boundary let through
Attributes on the spans that arrived
panels.description: The allowlist, made visible. core's schemas are the source of this list and `tests/validate.sh` in kit reads them off disk and compares both ways against the collector config — a name here that core does not allow, or one core allows and this list lacks, fails the gate. That is what makes 'the collector is the enforcement point' a fact rather than an intention.
